Arch translation from resource to bus address and bus resource accessor behavior
Locked versus unlocked PCIe capability implementations and their serialization scope
Real MSI MSI-X and vector allocation algorithms beyond stub fallbacks

findings.text: Host bridge object embeds a generic device plus root bus pointer with config access hooks for root and children, arch private data, numeric bus and domain identifiers, window plus DMA range plus root port lists, optional stream tracking under IDE, platform IRQ swizzle and mapping hooks, lifecycle hooks for release and device enable and disable and root port reset with release context, many single bit policy flags about reset delay and tags and MRRS and OS native use of AER and hotplug variants and PME and LTR and DPC and CXL errors and config preservation and window sizing and MSI domain and broken low power resume, a resource alignment hook, and a cache aligned trailing private area with bidirectional conversion helpers between bridge and private address.

Bus object links into global bus list and parent and child and device collections, points at upstream bridge device, keeps slot list under a dedicated mutex, holds fixed bridge aperture array plus routed address space list plus bus number resource, carries config access hooks and arch data and proc entry, numeric bus and primary identifiers with maximum and current speed, optional generic domain number, fixed length name, bridge control and inheritable flags, bridge and device objects, and single bit added and unsafe warning and flit mode state. Conversions exist between embedded device and bus and a helper builds a combined bus and function identifier.

Config access operations bundle five hooks: notification when a bus appears, notification when a bus disappears, mapping of a device function and offset to a mappable address, sized read into caller storage, and sized write from caller value. Reads and writes report status and take bus plus function plus offset plus width.

Driver object carries a name and a device match table that must be present for probing, lifecycle hooks for probe and remove and suspend and resume and shutdown, SR-IOV hooks for virtual function count and per function vector count and total vector query, a pointer to error handling hooks, two attribute group sets, an embedded generic driver with a null tolerant enclosing conversion, a runtime identifier collection, and a flag for driver managed DMA.

Error handling bundle provides separate callbacks for initial detection with channel state, MMIO only recovery stage, slot reset stage, reset preparation and completion notifications, final resume, and optional correctable error detail recording. A bus address interval holds inclusive start and end with a size helper adding one to the difference. Runtime identifier storage pairs a list with an index. MSI-X descriptor pairs kernel assigned vector with driver chosen entry number.

Recovery uses six ordered outcomes from no result through recoverable without reset, reset required, disconnected, fully recovered, and no AER driver. Normal progression is detection followed by MMIO enabled followed by slot reset followed by resume, with reset prepare and done bracketing function reset and a side path for correctable detail.

Unset domain is negative one. Only the low nibble of resource flags carries PCI region meaning. Exclusive config request capability marker equals two. Legacy IO span is 64K minus one and legacy memory span is 1M. VGA state change uses first bit for bridge and second bit for decodes.
BIOS style status zero means success. Six failure codes occupy a sparse range: unsupported function, bad vendor identifier, missing device, bad register, failed setting, and too small buffer.

Interrupt selection uses distinct low bits for legacy level, MSI, MSI-X, automatic affinity, and virtual. A combined mask covers the three transport types. Link power uses one bit pair for L0s directions, separate bits for L1 and deeper L1 sub variants under ASPM and PCI power management, plus a clock power bit, with aggregates for all ASPM levels and for every level including clock power.

Probe behavior uses single bit flags for full resource reassignment, full bus renumbering, probe only use of firmware setup, ISA alignment skipping, domain display in proc, domain zero compatibility, and broad PCIe scanning. Bus payload tuning has five ordered modes from untouched through default and safe and performance to peer to peer. Recovery outcomes are numbered one through six. Bus addresses are 64 bit in one build and 32 bit in the other. Ports disabled is logically true while native ports are logically false.

A bus without a parent is a root. A device is a bridge when its header kind denotes bridge or cardbus. VGA checks shifted class against two display values while generic display checks the base class field. CXL status mirrors a device flag. Upstream bridge resolves through the physical function and returns absent for root buses else the parent bridge device. Bridge iteration visits bus devices and executes its body only for bridges.

In the full build MSI is considered active when either MSI or MSI-X state is set; an alternate build always reports inactive. Interrupt kind prefers MSI-X over MSI over legacy, while a fallback build always reports legacy. Device active state is true when its enable counter is positive. Managed state mirrors a flag. INTx masking is available unless a broken quirk flag is set.

BIOS style error translation passes nonpositive values through as already native, maps six documented failure codes respectively to missing entry, inappropriate control, missing device, bad address, IO failure, and no space, and maps any other positive code to out of range.

Word capability updates for link and root control positions use a serialized path while other positions use an unserialized path; word and double word set and clear are degenerate forms of clear and set with one mask zero. Bus resource iteration covers fixed bridge apertures and list resources with two forms differing only in whether the loop index is caller supplied. Exclusive config reservation and release delegate to generic region handling with an exclusive marker. Bus address query translates a BAR resource through arch logic and returns its start.

Exact MSI-X request is a range request with equal bounds and normalizes success to zero while preserving negative status. Builds without MSI report not implemented for vector counts and enables and exact and range. One vector allocator grants a single legacy vector when legacy is allowed and exactly one is requested and a line exists, else reports no space; another build always reports no space and plain allocation delegates to affinity form with absent descriptor. Dynamic MSI-X support is false, dynamic allocation returns a not implemented marker map, free operations are empty, vector lookup warns once on nonzero index and otherwise returns the legacy line, affinity returns the possible set, and target speed programming reports unsupported.

INTx spec translation validates that the first cell lies between the first and last legacy pins inclusive, else invalid, and derives hardware number as offset from the first pin while leaving type untouched. Global PCI flags support overwrite, bitwise add, bitwise clear, and masked test. Slot assignment and cardbus bridge setup are empty in these fragments. PCI device check compares the generic bus pointer against the PCI bus type and physical function check further examines the owning device flag with false for non PCI.

Runtime identifier list and index are guarded by an embedded spinlock. Slot membership is guarded by a global slot mutex named in comments. Capability updates for selected link and root control registers must use the serialized locked form rather than the unlocked form.

Matching constructors cover exact vendor and device, exact vendor device subvendor subdevice, class plus mask with wildcards, vendor prefixed forms, vendor prefixed with sub identifiers, driver data carrying form, and driver override forms including a VFIO specialization. Registration helpers wrap generic module and builtin driver macros around PCI register and unregister.

Callable entry surfaces are config operation hooks, driver probe remove suspend resume shutdown and SR-IOV hooks, error handler stages, IRQ allocation and release and vector and affinity and type queries, MSI and MSI-X enable disable count restore and dynamic alloc free, capability clear set helpers, INTx mask and translation helpers, flag manipulators, and resource iteration macros that select an implementation by argument count.

Several MSI and vector paths are compile time stubs that return not implemented or no space or unsupported rather than performing allocation, so callers must handle those negatives. Legacy vector lookup warns once when asked beyond vector zero. Exclusive config reservation can collide if overlapping ranges are requested. Capability updates on the wrong path risk missing serialization.
Atomic counter read used to test device enable count is owned elsewhere.
